Choosing a model

models.Rmd

NMADTA implements two established Bayesian model families for networks of diagnostic tests. Both combine studies with different observed test sets, including studies with and without a reference standard.

Hierarchical model

nmadt.hierarchical() directly models accuracy parameters, including sensitivity and specificity, with between-study random effects. Pooled sensitivity and specificity are natural summary quantities. The model is described by Ma, Lian, Chu, Ibrahim, and Chen (2018), Biostatistics.

library(NMADTA)
data(dat.kang)

fit <- nmadt.hierarchical(
  nstu = 12, K = 2, data = dat.kang,
  testname = c("D-dimer", "Ultrasonography")
)

HSROC model

nmadt.hsroc() uses accuracy and threshold components. This parameterization is useful for considering differences in operating thresholds across studies and comparisons across the ROC space. The model is described by Lian, Hodges, and Chu (2019), Journal of the American Statistical Association.

fit_hsroc <- nmadt.hsroc(
  nstu = 12, K = 2, data = dat.kang,
  testname = c("D-dimer", "Ultrasonography"),
  n.adapt = 5000, n.iter = 50000, n.chains = 3
)

A common result interface

Both families return an object of class nmadt:

print(fit)
summary(fit)
plot(fit, type = "sroc")
plot(fit, type = "forest")
plot(fit, type = "density")
plot(fit, type = "contour")

Summaries include posterior estimates and intervals for sensitivity, specificity, prevalence, predictive values, and likelihood ratios. Each model has its own prior parameters; consult the reference before changing defaults.

Missing data and priors

Changing between hierarchical and HSROC formulations does not resolve uncertainty about why tests are missing. Regular functions use the MAR formulation; MNAR functions support sensitivity analysis.

Priors are specified on different scales in the two model families. Similar-looking default settings need not express equivalent prior information. For sparse networks or few reference-standard studies, examine identification, convergence, and prior sensitivity. The software article discusses these choices and the implementation’s limits.
